clean_methods: Central analytic strategy: Our approach involves creating "proxy measures" of cognitive abilities using predictive modeling techniques across different units of analysis, followed by commonality analyses to understand shared variance | Synthesis: This is the core pipeline that converts behavioral, neural, genetic, and environmental information into comparable cognitive-ability proxies and tests their shared variance with mental health.

Data foundation: We will use data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, examining children aged 9-10 at baseline and 11-12 at two-year follow-up | Synthesis: Provides the longitudinal, multi-site pediatric sample needed to estimate and validate the proposed proxies across development.

Behavioral cognitive target: We will operationalize cognitive abilities as a latent variable (g-factor) representing behavioral performance across six cognitive tasks using confirmatory factor analysis | Synthesis: Defines the behavioral cognitive-ability construct that all predictive proxy measures are intended to represent.

Mental-health outcome domain: Mental health will be assessed through emotional and behavioral problems (Child Behaviour Checklist) and temperaments (BIS/BAS and UPPS-P scales) | Synthesis: Specifies the mental-health variables used to examine the cognitive-ability-mental-health relationship.

Primary shared-variance inference: We will extract predicted values from each predictive model as proxy measures of cognitive abilities and conduct four sets of commonality analyses using random-intercept linear mixed models | Synthesis: Tests the shared variance among mental-health, neuroimaging, polygenic, and environmental proxies, including the four specified pairwise and comprehensive analyses.

Generalizability validation: We will implement nested leave-one-site-out cross-validation to ensure generalizability across different sites, treating one of 21 sites as a test set while using the remaining sites for training. Within each training set, we will apply 10-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter tuning | Synthesis: Ensures that predictive proxies are not site-specific and that hyperparameters are selected without leakage.

Mental-health proxy model: We will use Partial Least Squares (PLS) to predict cognitive abilities from mental health features, testing CBCL and temperament measures separately and combined | Synthesis: Creates the mental-health-derived proxy measure used in commonality analyses.

Neuroimaging proxy model: We will implement opportunistic stacking with two layers: (1) set-specific layer using Elastic Net to predict cognitive abilities from each of 45 neuroimaging feature sets, and (2) stacking layer using Random Forest to combine predictions across all sets. This approach will handle missing neuroimaging data while maximizing predictive performance | Synthesis: Creates the multimodal neuroimaging proxy from task-fMRI, resting-state fMRI, structural MRI, and diffusion tensor imaging.

Genetic feature construction: We will calculate PGS based on three large-scale genome-wide association studies on cognitive abilities | Synthesis: Constructs the polygenic-score features used to test whether the cognitive-ability-mental-health relationship is represented at the genetic level.

Genetic proxy model: We will use Elastic Net to predict cognitive abilities from three PGS definitions, selecting optimal PGS thresholds within training sets and controlling for population stratification using genetic principal components | Synthesis: Creates the polygenic proxy measure while reducing ancestry-related confounding.

Environmental feature space: we will include 44 features covering socio-demographics, lifestyles, and developmental adverse events | Synthesis: Defines the environmental variables used to test whether environmental factors explain the cognitive-ability-mental-health relationship.

Environmental proxy model: We will apply PLS to predict cognitive abilities from socio-demographic, lifestyle, and developmental adverse event features, handling missing values through imputation | Synthesis: Creates the environmental proxy measure used in commonality analyses.

Confounding and dependency controls: We will control for biological sex, age, and medication effects by residualizing these variables from observed cognitive abilities and proxy measures. Family structure will be accounted for in the mixed-effects models, with families nested within sites | Synthesis: Reduces confounding and accounts for family and site structure in the commonality analyses.

Longitudinal stability: We will repeat all analyses at both time points (baseline and two-year follow-up) to demonstrate the stability of our findings across this developmental period. We will use the same CFA model for cognitive abilities across time points and apply consistent standardization procedures to ensure comparability | Synthesis: Tests whether the proposed neurobiological and environmental representations remain stable over the two-year developmental window.

Model evaluation and interpretability: We will evaluate predictive performance using Pearson correlation coefficients, coefficient of determination (R²), mean absolute error, and root mean square error. Feature importance will be assessed through PLS loadings, Elastic Net coefficients, and SHAP values for Random Forest models | Synthesis: Quantifies predictive accuracy and identifies which features drive each proxy model.
